subtopic: Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading
question_en: Aggregate bond indexes are most likely to:
option_a: have less turnover than broad equity indexes.
option_b: have large weights in sovereign bonds.
option_c: include all bond sectors in a single currency.
explanation_en: Aggregate indexes contain a broad selection of bonds across sectors and currencies. Because sovereign governments are the largest issuers of bonds, they typically have the largest weight in broad bond indexes. Because bonds mature, they must be replaced in indexes more frequently than equities.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading
question_en: An analyst has been tasked by his boss to review several bonds from issuers that used to carry investment-grade ratings, but have recently been downgraded to below investment grade. The bonds in this analyst's portfolio are best described as:
explanation_en: Fallen angels is the term for bonds associated with issuers that previously held investment-grade ratings, that have since been downgraded to below investment grade. Neither of the other terms are used to describe these bonds. Yields would increase as the bond is downgraded to below investment grade.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading
question_en: Which type of issuer is most likely to issue bonds by auction?
explanation_en: Many national governments use auctions to issue sovereign bonds. Corporate bonds are typically issued in an underwriting or private placement process while municipal bonds are typically issued in a negotiated or underwritten process.

subtopic: Reading 51 Fixed-Income Issuance and Trading
question_en: A bond is quoted at 96.25 bid and 96.75 ask. Based only on this information, this bond is most likely:
explanation_en: The spread between the bid and ask prices is one-half percent of par, which most likely reflects an illiquid market for this bond. Bonds with liquid secondary markets typically have bid-ask spreads of approximately 10 to 12 basis points.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: The interest rate on excess reserves borrowed by one bank from another bank is most accurately described as a(n):
explanation_en: Required reserves are deposits with a country's central bank. Banks that deposit more than the required amount with the central bank are said to have excess reserves and may lend these to other banks. This lending is said to take place in the central bank funds market and the interest rates on such loans are known as central bank funds rates.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: Which of the following debt covenants is most likely to be found with a high-yield debt issuance?
option_a: A minimum dividend payment of $5 per share to common stockholders.
option_b: A debt-to-equity ratio that cannot go below 40%.
option_c: A cap of $20 million on total debt outstanding.
explanation_en: Debt covenants are put in place to protect debt investors. A cap on the total amount of debt a company can have outstanding will protect current debt investors from the company borrowing more money and putting current obligation interest and principal payments at risk. The debt-to-equity ratio debt covenant will likely be a maximum (not a minimum) threshold. Dividend payments are likely to be maximum amounts not to be exceeded, rather than minimum amounts.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: Reduced rollover risk resulting from standardization is a benefit available to which type of corporate bond issuer?
explanation_en: Investment-grade issues are standardized (similar across different issues) and typically issued across multiple maturities, which reduces rollover risk (the risk that maturing debt will have to be replaced with new debt at higher interest rates). High-yield debt is not standardized and often matures earlier than investment-grade debt. Short-term debt will carry more rollover risk.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: The credit spread is 5% of the yield on Bond A, 10% of the yield on Bond B, and 30% of the yield on Bond C. Bond C is most likely:
explanation_en: For high-yield bonds, credit spreads are likely to be a larger proportion of yield than they are for investment-grade bonds and government bonds.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: Assuming a normal yield curve environment, higher yields must be offered by corporate issuers on bonds that mature in 20 years compared with those that mature in 10 years, if the 20-year bonds are considered:
explanation_en: In a normal yield curve environment where bond yields are higher for longer-dated bond maturities, both investment-grade and high-yield corporate issuers need to offer higher yields on bonds with longer maturities.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: Compared to a term repurchase agreement, an overnight repurchase agreement is most likely to have a:
option_a: higher repo rate and repo margin.
option_b: lower repo rate and higher repo margin.
option_c: lower repo rate and repo margin.
explanation_en: Both the repo rate and the repo margin tend to be higher for longer repo terms. Therefore an overnight repo should have a lower repo rate and a lower repo margin than a term (i.e., longer than overnight) repo.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: The interbank funds market is most accurately described as:
option_a: banks’ borrowing of reserves from the central bank.
option_b: trading of negotiable certicates of deposit.
option_c: unsecured short-term loans from one bank to another.
explanation_en: The interbank funds market refers to short-term unsecured loans between banks. It does not refer to trading of negotiable certificates of deposit. Borrowing from the central bank is said to occur in the central bank funds market.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: Which of the following statements regarding repurchase agreements is most accurate?
option_a: Greater demand for the underlying security results in a lower repo margin.
option_b: Higher credit rating of the underlying collateral results in a higher repo rate.
option_c: Lower credit rating of the underlying collateral results in a lower repo margin.
explanation_en: Other things equal, the repo margin (percent difference between the market value of the collateral and the loan amount) is lower if the collateral is in greater demand. The repo margin and repo rate (the annualized percent difference between the sale price and repurchase price of the collateral) are inversely related to the credit quality of the collateral.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 52 Fixed-Income Markets for Corporate Issuers
question_en: A repurchase agreement is described as a "reverse repo" if:
option_a: a bond dealer is the lender.
option_b: collateral is delivered to the lender and returned to the borrower.
option_c: the repurchase price is lower than the sale price.
explanation_en: Bond dealers frequently use repurchase agreements as sources of funding. When a bond dealer enters a repo as the lender instead of the borrower, the agreement is referred to as a reverse repo.

subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: Bonds issued by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) are most accurately described as:
explanation_en: Supranational bonds are issued by multilateral organizations such as the IMF. Quasi-government bonds are issued by agencies established or sponsored by national government. Non-sovereign government bonds are issued by state, provincial, and local government or municipal entities.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: Relative to the yields on nonsovereign bonds, sovereign bond yields may be lower because of the:
option_a: requirement to distribute them in an auction format.
option_b: greater risk associated with their issuers.
option_c: regulatory requirements, forcing some financial institutions to hold government debt.
explanation_en: Some financial institutions may be required to hold government bonds, which can lower their yields relative to nonsovereign debt. Sovereign debt tends to carry less risk than other types of debt (therefore, lower yield), and the requirement to distribute them in an auction format is not a primary cause of the yield differences between sovereign and nonsovereign debt.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: The cutoff yield associated with a government bond issuance is best described as the yield of the successful competitive bid with the:
explanation_en: The cutoff yield is defined as the yield of the successful competitive bid with the lowest price. All investors will pay the price associated with this yield in a single-price auction, whereas in a multiple-price auction, successful bidders will pay the price they bid.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: Fixed income classifications by geography most likely include:
explanation_en: Classifying fixed income securities as developed market or emerging market bonds is an example of classification by geography. Supranational bonds are a classification by type of issuer. Municipal bonds are a classification by type of issuer or by taxable status.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: The Federal Reserve Bank of the United States will most likely work with primary dealers to enact which of the following transactions?
option_a: Contractionary scal policy through the decrease in government spending.
option_b: Expansionary monetary policy through the purchase of Treasury securities.
option_c: Expansionary monetary policy through the sale of Treasury securities.
explanation_en: The Federal Reserve Bank of the United States enacts monetary (not fiscal) policy. Primary dealers will serve as counterparties for the purchase (expansionary) or sale (contractionary) of Treasury securities for the purpose of enacting monetary policy. Fiscal policy does involve government spending and taxes, but that is not executed by the Federal Reserve Bank.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Fixed income\Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: PD Bank is a primary dealer that submits bids for third parties at public auctions. The bids are most likely for the purchase of debt securities issued by:
explanation_en: Public auctions are used by sovereign issuers to issue government debt securities, and primary dealers are financial institutions (like PD Bank, in this case) that make competitive bids, submit bids on behalf of third parties, and act as counterparties to the central bank in monetary policy transactions. Corporations and not-for-profits are not using auction formats.

subtopic: Reading 53 Fixed-Income Markets for Government Issuers
question_en: A government entity is using a single-price auction to issue new debt in the hopes of minimizing yield volatility. The price that all investors will pay under this format is associated with the:
explanation_en: The cutoff yield is defined as the yield of the successful competitive bid with the lowest price. All investors will pay the price associated with this yield in a single-price auction.
